title: Skill signature role brief & interview evidence mapper
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, actionable role brief designed to surface the specific skill signature we care about for mid-senior backend platform engineers (inference infra focus). The doc intentionally connects: (1) what successful work looks like, (2) concrete interview exercises that surface evidence, (3) an interviewer rubic for consistent scoring, and (4) first-90-day onboarding milestones + access checklist to shorten time-to-impact. Use as a reusable template for similar technical roles.

Role summary (1-liner):
Build and operate the inference-serving surface: reliable, cost-conscious GPU orchestration and runtime improvements that reduce token latency and unit cost for production workloads.

Skill signature (top 5 observable behaviors we hire for):
1) Systems reasoning under resource constraints — designs that trade latency vs cost with clear measurements.
2) Latency-first debugging — isolates tail-latency sources across networking, batching, and KV caches.
3) Safe rollout and rollback hygiene — incremental deploys, canary metrics and automatic fallback.
4) Experimental quant/ops tuning — understands quantization and batching knobs and validates on representative workloads.
5) Cross-functional communication — translates infra trade-offs for product/CS and documents runbooks.

What success looks like (first 6 months):
- Reduce p50/p95 token latency for a high-throughput route by 10–25% while keeping cost within target range.
- Ship a rollout policy with canarying and automatic fallback that prevented at least one incident.
- Deliver two performance regressions prevented by a prompt-driven eval + CI check.

Interview flow and mapping to evidence: (45–75m candidate loop)
1) Intro + context (5m) — quick role alignment; assess communication clarity.
2) System design (25–30m) — prompt: "Design a multi-tenant inference serving architecture for mixed-latency workloads. Show how you route requests, handle KV cache, and support fallbacks."
   Evidence sought: architecture diagrams, trade-offs on batching vs latency, fallback strategies, metrics to monitor.
3) Debugging / root-cause exercise (15–20m) — give a short flamechart + logs where p95 spikes intermittently. Candidate triages live, proposes experiments, and identifies likely root cause.
   Evidence: prioritization of hypotheses, testable experiments, instrumentation asks.
4) Short live coding (15–20m) — implement a simple rate-limiter / token-bucket or a micro-batcher pseudo-implementation in preferred language.
   Evidence: correctness, edge cases, test thinking.
5) Behavioral / closeout (10m) — ask for trade-off stories and communication examples.

Interview tasks and scoring rubric (0–4 scale per dimension; anchor examples):
- Systems reasoning (0: unclear or impossible design; 4: concrete measurable design with failovers and metrics).
- Practical debugging (0: cannot form testable hypotheses; 4: clear, prioritized RCA plan with instrumentation).
- Safety/rollout hygiene (0: no rollback plan; 4: canary + metrics + automated fallback described).
- Coding correctness (0: incorrect or unsafe; 4: correct, handles edge cases, test-oriented).
- Communication (0: unclear, unstructured; 4: concise, stakeholder-aware, runsheet provided).

Pass threshold guidance:
- Minimum 3 on at least 3 of the 5 dimensions, and no score of 0 on safety/communication. Use hiring committee to weigh borderline cases (two 2s + one 4, etc.).

Interview exercise artifacts (what to collect from candidate):
- One-page architecture sketch (photo or whiteboard photo).
- Short bullet write-up (200–400 words) describing rollout plan and fallback policy.
- Small code snippet for the rate-limiter/micro-batcher.

Calibration notes for interviewers (quick cheatsheet):
- If candidate proposes a pure-queueing approach without KV cache — probe for prompt reuse and cold-start cost.
- If the candidate drops quantization entirely, ask about model accuracy trade-offs and validation datasets.
- On debugging, look for experiments that are cheap to run first (config checks, telemetry) before invasive changes.

Onboarding & first-90-day checklist (practical items + acceptance criteria):
Week 0–1 (access + quick wins):
- Access: git, infra dashboard + read-only, deploy pipeline access request, Slack channels, internal runbooks.
- Quick win: reproduce a flaky Canary incident locally or in staging and write a short post-mortem draft.
Acceptance: able to run local integration tests and describe the deploy flow end-to-end.

Month 1 (ramp + instrumentation):
- Deliver: one small improvement (config tuning, alert fix, or dashboard) that reduces false positives or improved SLO visibility.
- Pairing: 3 shadowing sessions with oncall/serving-runtime, one cross-team sync with product.
Acceptance: demonstrates ability to interpret core metrics (p50/p95, queue length, batching efficiency).

Month 2 (feature + ownership):
- Deliver: own a small route or policy (canary rules, cost cap) and propose a measurable experiment.
- Documentation: publish a concise runbook for the owned route.
Acceptance: team review of runbook and green signal on proposed experiment design.

Month 3 (impact + scale):
- Deliver: experiment run and analysis; propose next-phase scaling/quantization work.
Acceptance: measurable improvement or validated learnings that lead to a follow-up ticket.

Access matrix (minimal for first week, who to ping):
- Repo access: infra-team (request via internal access form)
- Staging GPU clusters: infra-sre (temporary credentials request)
- Metrics/dashboards: observability team (read+comment)
- Deploy pipelines: release-eng (deployer role request)
- Cost dashboards: finance ops (read-only)

Mentor pairing & checkpoints:
- Primary mentor: senior platform engineer (scheduled 1:1 twice weekly first month, weekly thereafter).
- Oncall buddy: rotate with site reliability engineer for shadow shifts first 6 weeks.
- Checkpoints: 2-week sync (people-ops + manager), 6-week review (engineering lead), 12-week review (manager + mentor).

Template: interviewer feedback form (copy into interview tool)
- Role: [text]
- Date: [date]
- Dimensions (rate 0–4 with notes): systems reasoning / debugging / safety / coding / communication
- Red flags (free text)
- Green signals (free text)
- Recommendation: Strong hire | Hire | No hire | Defer

Handoff to manager on offer acceptance:
- Required before day 1: checklist of repos, runbook links, mentor/buddy names, first-week priorities, and access status for each item.
- Suggested first-week schedule: 1) infra orientation, 2) runbook reading & quick win 3) shadow oncall.

Open questions & notes to people-ops team (to iterate):
- Should we formalize a small test harness that can run candidate micro-batcher code against a synthetic latency workload? (pro: objective measurement; con: maintenance).
- Proposal: keep this template as a Living Doc and add role-specific examples for quant/ops, runtime, and orchestration hires.

Appendix: quick example interview prompt (copy/paste)
"You are joining Redwood Inference's serving-runtime team. We run multi-tenant GPU pools with mixed latency SLAs. Design an architecture that minimizes tail latency for chat workloads while controlling cost for batch embeddings. Include caching strategies, a deploy/rollout approach, and a rollback policy. Be prepared to sketch major components and explain what you would measure."

Endnotes:
- This doc is intentionally concise and pragmatic; treat it as an operational artifact that gets updated after every hire loop.
- Owner: People Ops (Maya Thompson) — please add post-hire notes and calibration outcomes to CONFLUENCE-5482.
